I haven't moved away from reddit, or to whoaverse. I just wanted to make this a better place by suggesting what I think is best for a website like this.

I didn't come here because of the vote change. I very much agree with the change.

Either way, removing karma is very different from hiding the vote count on posts. Getting rid of karma has no direct effect on a person's experience while browsing the website. The only thing that'll change (for the better, in my opinion), is that people will stop forcing "funny", quirky comments or posts just to gain some imaginary, useless points.

I mean, right now, there is no chance that you'll actually be able to speak your mind on reddit, unless it co-aligns with what the rest of reddit think that week. If you do do it, your comment will get tons of downvotes, which is something a lot of people want to avoid - because karma.

I don't know; I have no problems speaking my mind whatsoever on Reddit or on whoaverse, myself. If anything, I find it easier than on social media where I tend to be concerned with whether certain friends, family members, etc., will be offended for some bizarre reason or another.

It's actually way more freeing to be on a place where I am anonymous and don't have to worry about all that crap.

I mean, if the issue is that you can't be as hateful/bigoted/profane/insulting as you want to be without getting downvoted to hell- if that's what you mean by "speaking your mind," then I have to say, you're almost never going to be able to find a place where you can be as offensive as you want and people will just agree with you or won't disagree.

I've never been downvoted to oblivion, as people have claimed, by speaking my mind, as long as I've been respectful of others and presented a coherent and thoughtful perspective.

(In case you were wondering) I did disagree with the decision to the hide the fuzzed vote count, but actually more because of the way it was handled and the obvious lack of transparency about the entire thing, plus the apparent lack of response or justification from the admins given the backlash from the community.

I came here to hopefully find a place where the community is listened to, that isn't as much controlled by commercial interests. Still using Reddit, too, for some things, of course.

EDIT: I wasn't trying to say you are being offensive or post offensive things; sorry if I worded that wrong. Just that that's the only way I can imagine someone having to worry at all about getting way downvoted.

Go ahead and check out bottoms of some big reddit threads, and see how many of those downvoted comments are just opinions reddit disagrees with.

From what I've seen over the course of years, a lot of them are usually just people expressing their opinions, but since the majority of reddit's userbase disagrees with them, no one gets to see those opinions, because they end up at the very bottom.

Removing karma is not going to get rid of that, but that was not the reason why I posted this thread.

Yeah, reddit gives you more freedom in freely expressing yourself, but it could be better if people didn't care for their karma.

It creates nothing but problems. I think Whoaverse would be much better off without karma.

I'm going to start off by saying that I only have a month of Reddit experience and barely joined WhoaVerse a few days ago, so my opinion may not be the most credible. But, I've had this discussion before in a Reddit argument and I'll say it again here: I don't care about 'karma'. They are imaginary points that don't affect my life.

That said, I'd like to mention that I think the imaginary points are cool. They tell me how helpful my contributions have been to the community. 'Karmawhoring' is an issue with the user, not the website. I never understood the concept because, as far as I know, these points have no use. Hoarding these points yields no visible benefits.

I may be overlooking something as someone who's still new to this 'imaginary points' thing, but I've never been afraid to voice my opinion, no matter how controversial it may be. So, I don't think it creates noticeable problems and I certainly think it's a cool feature to have on here.
